gloss: for a long time; for many years

definitions.gloss: for a long time; for a long while; for many years
definitions.explanation: An adverb indicating that something has continued for a long period. Slightly formal and polite in tone, often used when acknowledging someone's patience or long-standing relationship.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}らくお{待|ま}たせしました。
examples.english: Thank you for waiting so long. (Sorry to have kept you waiting.)

examples.japanese: {長|なが}らくご{愛顧|あいこ}いただき、ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for your long patronage.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}らく{営業|えいぎょう}してまいりましたが、{今月|こんげつ}{末|まつ}をもちまして{閉店|へいてん}いたします。
examples.english: We have been in business for a long time, but we will be closing at the end of this month.

notes:
USAGE:
{長|なが}らく is a formal, polite adverb often used in set phrases expressing gratitude or apology for something that has lasted a long time. It is very common in customer service, business, and ceremonial language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長|なが}らくお{待|ま}たせしました (sorry to have kept you waiting)
- {長|なが}らくご{愛顧|あいこ}いただき (thank you for your long patronage)
- {長|なが}らくお{世話|せわ}になりました (thank you for your support over the years)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {長|なが}らく: for a long time (formal, polite)
- {長|なが}い{間|あいだ}: for a long time (neutral, everyday)
- ずっと: all along, the whole time (casual, emphasizes continuity)
